newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's King Hussein to allow Hamas leader back.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's King Hussein to allow Hamas leader back.

text.p: King Hussein has said he will allow Mousa Abu Marzook, political leader of the militant Islamic group Hamas jailed in the United States, to return to Jordan, a government minister said on Wednesday.
"His Majesty, for humanitarian reasons, has approved allowing Abu Marzook to come back to Jordan without any obligations," Information Minister Samir Mutawae told Reuters.
Mutawae did not say when Abu Marzook, who was expelled from Jordan in June 1995 in a move aimed at improving ties with Israel and the Palestinian Authority, might return.
Abu Marzook was arrested in New York a few weeks after he left Jordan. Israel sought his extradition saying he was responsible for bomb attacks which killed scores of Israelis.

But security officials said in February that Israel, fearing a wave of violence if Abu Marzook were extradited to an Israeli prison, was examining a deal with Jordan and the United States to send him to Amman in return for a promise to shun violence.
Mutawae did not say if Abu Marzook had made such a pledge, or whether Israel and the United States had formally agreed to the move.

"Anybody who comes here as a political refugee has to abide by the laws and regulations of the country. So if he wants to accept His Majesty's gesture he would have to abide by our law," Mutawae said.
